week.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
week.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. week.description: Kronos: A Foundation Model for the Language of Financial Markets

month.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
month.readme: See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level. Join the Reverse Engineering Community See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites.

month.description: ArtCraft is an intentional crafting engine for artists, designers, and filmmakers
month.readme: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7339bd09-3e0d-44a7-a024-af9de64e4c11 Watch the two-minute ArtCraft demo on YouTube ArtCraft is the IDE for interactive AI image and video creation. month.readme: A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness. The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

month.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
month.readme: Tool for automatic executables porting to Linux and Windows. The relinker-only build runs on macOS, including Apple silicon. Web converter - files stay on your device. Includes a relinker that converts executable to the target system's native format and implementations of system prx libraries suitable for dynamic linking. No emulation or separate runtime process.

month.description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative, voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
month.readme: 🎉 100,000 GitHub stars, thank you! AI voice studio. On your device. Clone, design, dub, dictate, transcribe and narrate in 646 languages. Runs on your laptop, desktop, servers, phone, tablets and more Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice. Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original. Describe a voice in words and generate it. Choose your engines and download only the models you need.

month.description: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.
month.readme: Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents. HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The HyperFrames Studio app is free to use as well; its Pro plan adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent?

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app (iOS, Android), web app and Electron-based desktop app. Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them. Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents.

month.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
month.readme: Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it. Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together. Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents.

new.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
new.readme: dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person. It is also a way of working with an agent: take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.

new.description: Craft Anything: understand how any software works, and craft your own.
new.readme: See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust. Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools, has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it. A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

new.readme: 244 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code. Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. new.readme: TotK Recomp is a static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native x86-64 application for Windows and Linux (docs/architecture.md). Early development. The game is playable on Windows and Linux; visual bugs and crashes are still expected. Report problems as issues, following CONTRIBUTING.md.

new.description: VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator
new.readme: Eglantine is a free and opensource (FOSS) Switch 2 emulator, derived from Eden, Yuzu and Sudachi - started by developer Camille LaVey. It's written in C++ with portability in mind, with builds for Windows, Linux and macOS The emulator is capable of running Mario Kart World at decent/full speed depending on specs and configurations, and Splatoon Raiders at variable performances A list of supported games will be available in future. Please be patient.

new.description: VERY experimental Nintendo Switch 2 emulator
new.readme: Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the official Lichii website to find games and compare community compatibility reports. Published builds belong on this fork's releases page.

new.readme: A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. terminal-mac is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. new.readme: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick. hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install Downloads from official sources. It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. Makes room safely.

new.readme: Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. new.description: Pika H3 Flex: video and audio generation inference
new.readme: Built for professional iteration. Pika H3 Flex is a post-trained H3 model, designed to give professional creators the flexibility and speed to explore with precision. Optimized for greater control, it generates video with synchronized audio in six sampling steps and supports up to 12 reference inputs, with shot direction through references and prompts. Pika’s hosted API extends this workflow with 1080p, 2K and 4K video generation, audio stems and prompt enhancement.

new.description: Blazing-fast native notes app for macOS & Windows. Rust + GPUI, local-first, compatible with Feishu/Lark DocxXML.
new.readme: A fast, quiet, local notes app. Drawn natively with Rust + GPUI. Your notes stay on your computer, stored in the Feishu (Lark) DocxXML format. Linux support is experimental and currently built from source; see the Linux instructions and validation limits. ⚡ Fast, the native kind of fast. The whole interface is drawn on the GPU by Rust and GPUI. No WebView, no Electron. In a one-million-character document, typing, deleting and scrolling all stay under 6 ms per frame at P95. 🔒 Local-first. Your files are yours.

constraints.note: Official actions with a document that make AI harder, slower or costlier to train, publish, host, reach or buy. New ones first, then those with a date still ahead or seen in the last week; every action stays in the register at data/v1/constraints.json. Magpie reports the mechanism, not the politics.

gap.method: Lag is how long before the open model's release a closed model first reached the same Capabilities Index score. Today's figure measures from that closed model to today, so it grows until an open model moves the frontier.

hardware.finding: GeForce RTX 5090 decodes fastest; DGX Spark fits the biggest models
hardware.method: Ceiling = memory bandwidth / 16 GB of weights; real decode runs below it. Fits = 80% of memory at 0.55 GB per billion parameters (4-bit). List prices are the maker's own store; street prices are dated checks of a major retailer.
